reason: The speed numbers are exactly what I'm missing, so I'd install it and throw a few hundred RAWs at it. But the listing says nothing about star ratings, labels or XMP, so I can't cull in it and I can't make it my default over Bridge.
why_switch_or_not: I'd try it for first-look checks of RAW+JPG pairs and for opening one-off files without waiting for Bridge or Photoshop to start. The 40-50 ms next/back and the separate RAW and JPG entries are what I want. I wouldn't switch fully, because my catalogue and XMP stay in Lightroom and Bridge, and I see nothing about ratings, colour labels or reading and writing XMP. If I rate in NuViewer and it doesn't reach my catalogue, the culling is wasted.
current_app_pros: Bridge, Lightroom and Photoshop read my XMP and ratings, and the colour management is trusted and consistent with what I deliver. Camera Raw develops my RAWs correctly and my 200,000-picture catalogue lives there.
current_app_pains: Opening heavy Adobe apps just to look at one file is slow, and Bridge thumbnails and previews lag when I flick through a shoot. I notice every half-second wait, and I do it hundreds of times a day.
objection: My colour management, catalogue and XMP workflow must not change. NuViewer develops RAW itself and has its own sidecar edit file, so I don't know if its colour matches Camera Raw or if it would touch, ignore or conflict with my XMP. It's also a 0.4.1 from one person, so I don't know if it survives 200,000 files on a drive.
would_change_my_mind: Reading and writing star ratings and colour labels in standard XMP sidecars that Bridge and Lightroom see, plus a RAW render I can check side by side with Camera Raw that is close enough for culling.
